task: Sacroiliac (SI) joint pelvic-ring load transfer and form/force-closure stability mechanism -- reproduce the measured small-but-nonzero SI ROM (~2-4 deg / ~1-2mm), show BOTH a rigid-pelvis (zero-ROM) null AND a free-hinge (large-ROM) null are inconsistent with it; show force closure is load-bearing (reducing muscle/ligament compression measurably reduces stiffness/increases shear laxity); show nutation increases with load (self-locking, not runaway); test 3 perturbation adversaries (peripartum relaxin laxity, SI fusion, pelvic-ring fracture load-path disruption).

vleeming_schuenke_2019_master_mechanism_.numbers: VERBATIM (full mechanism statement): 'If the sacrum would fit in the pelvis with perfect form closure, no lateral compressional forces would be needed to maintain stability. However, such a construction would make mobility practically impossible ... Structures that contribute to SIJ stability via form closure include (1) the configuration of the interfacing joint surfaces, along with dorsocranial wedging of the sacrum into the ilia; (2) the corresponding ridges and grooves ... and resultant high coefficient of friction; and (3) the integrity of the binding ligaments ... In order for force closure to be effective, sacral nutation must occur and is considered to be anticipatory for joint loading. Sacral nutation results in tensing all of the dorsal SIJ ligaments (interosseous, dorsal sacroiliac) with the exception of one, the long dorsal ligament (LDL) ... As a result, the posterior ilium are pressed together causing an increase in SIJ compression.' THE master mechanism summary paper -- states both nulls' inconsistency and the self-locking mechanism explicitly, in the field's own words, most mature (2019) statement of the theory.

DECISIVE pelvic-ring-fracture load-path-coupling experiment (gate G9): sectioning the anterior ring measurably changes motion at the separate posterior SI complex, under a realistic 500N cyclic load, n=8, fully independent (Toronto) of the Rotterdam program.

symmetric_qc_open_items: Common-mode source risk for G5/G6/G7 (Sec.4): the decisive direct-manipulation mechanism experiments (cadaveric ligament-section, EMG belt-substitution, nutation-tension buckle-transducer) all originate from one ~30-year Rotterdam/Erasmus University research program with heavily overlapping authorship (Vleeming, Snijders, Stoeckart, Buyruk, Pool-Goudzwaard, Damen, van Wingerden). No fully independent, unconnected laboratory was found this session to have directly replicated these specific experiments. Partially mitigated by the geometric necessity argument (Coulomb F=muN, independent of any lab's interpretation) and by Nordberg 2021's fully independent tribological replication of the surface-mechanism half -- not closed.

G1's own near-miss (Sec.2): the single smallest individual rotation reading across Sturesson 1989's 25 patients (0.8 deg) is only 4.0x the noise floor, below this gate's own pre-registered 5x bar. Scored on each study's headline mean (the standard statistic each paper reports), not the smallest individual value -- both numbers disclosed.

Buyruk 1995b's abstract confirms a SIGNIFICANT difference across intact/screwed/ligaments-cut but does not itself state the per-condition ranking/direction or magnitude -- full text paywalled, not recovered this session. The predicted direction (cutting ligaments reduces stiffness) comes from theory (Pool-Goudzwaard 1998, Vleeming & Schuenke 2019) and is echoed by the separate Snijders 1998 EMG result, not confirmed by this abstract's text directly.

No wedge half-angle was independently measured or derived (Sec.3) -- 'dorsocranial wedging' is the field's own verified descriptive language (PMID 31218826), not an angle this doc computed from CT/morphometric raw data (unavailable for live fetch this session).

The self-locking loop's demand-side growth rate was not independently derived (Sec.5) -- rests on Sturesson 2000's net-outcome RSA measurement, not a separately re-derived rate comparison between shear-capacity growth and shear-demand growth.
Relaxin's specific mechanical contribution is confounded with pregnancy weight gain, postural change, and vascular effects within the cited studies (Sec.6) -- named, not resolved.

SI fusion's ROM-reduction number (Lindsey 2015) is computational (FE model), not an in-vivo RSA measurement of an actually-fused joint -- the model is described by its own authors as 'experimentally validated,' not independently re-validated this session.
Small, geographically narrow sample sizes throughout the classic biomechanical literature (n=4-25 for cadaveric/RSA studies) -- typical for the era/field, a real instance-space caveat.
5 of 28 citations are pre-abstract-era PubMed records (title/PMID/DOI verified live, no abstract text available): Weisl 1954, Tile 1988.

Vleeming 1990 Part II's exact numeric friction coefficient was not recovered (abstract states the relationship qualitatively) -- a targeted live search found only Nordberg 2021's relative (28% vs knee) figure, used throughout instead of a fabricated absolute value.
This doc did not build or modify any OpenSim model -- Sec.8's finding is a read-only grep against existing files; the proposed SI joint DOF (Sec.10) is a scoped next step, not executed this session.
